one_liner: Header-only C++ from_chars for float/double/int; 3-5x faster than glibc strtod, exact IEEE rounding.
what_it_does: Parses ASCII decimal strings into float, double, and integer types with exact, correctly-rounded IEEE-754 results, mirroring the C++17 std::from_chars signature while only requiring C++11. It is largely drop-in for strtod/std::from_chars call sites: from_chars(first, last, value, fmt) returns a from_chars_result{ptr, ec}, never throws, and never allocates. A separate from_chars_advanced entry point adds locale-style decimal separators, JSON/JavaScript/Fortran number-format modes, and UTF-16/UTF-32 input.
how_it_is_fast: Uses the Eisel-Lemire algorithm (named directly in a comment in include/fast_float/parse_number.h): a fast path that combines the decimal significand with precomputed power-of-five tables to compute the correctly-rounded binary value from one or two 64-bit multiplications (compute_product_approximation in decimal_to_binary.h). When that approximation cannot be proven correct, which is rare, it falls back to exact big-integer digit comparison (bigint.h / digit_comparison.h) instead of a slow generic parser, so the common case stays branch-light and allocation-free.
when_to_use: Parsing large volumes of floats/doubles from text (JSON, CSV, scientific/columnar data) where strtod or std::from_chars throughput is a bottleneck
Header-only C++11+ codebases that want a from_chars-shaped API without adding a build dependency
Need locale-independent, correctly-rounded parsing with round-to-even tie-breaking
Need JSON, JavaScript-literal, or Fortran-literal number grammars without hand-rolling the format checks
when_not_to_use: Need long double parsing - unsupported; only float, double, and fixed-width float16/32/64/bfloat16 are covered
Need hexadecimal floating-point literals - decimal format only
Building with -ffast-math: infinity()/NaN handling is documented-incompatible in open issue #397 (unresolved as of 2026-09-24)
Only parsing a handful of floats and every byte of compile time / include overhead matters, since it is a template-heavy header-only include vs. a plain libc call
Want locale-aware parsing out of the box - the default from_chars is locale-independent; locale behavior requires the separate from_chars_advanced API

integration.min_toolchain: C++11 for the core library (CMakeLists.txt sets FASTFLOAT_CXX_STANDARD 11 by default); C++20 needed for constexpr parsing; CMake 3.14+ for the build/install targets
integration.platforms: Windows/MSVC, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD per README; supports big- and little-endian, 32-bit and 64-bit systems; CI also exercises ARM, RISC-V, and s390x (big-endian)
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly, but from_chars/from_chars_advanced are stateless, non-throwing, and non-allocating (per README), with no shared mutable state, so concurrent calls on independent buffers are safe
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial - explain: call shape tracks C++17 std::from_chars (same argument order, chars_format enum), but the result is returned via from_chars_result{ptr, ec} rather than strtod's return-value+errno+endptr convention, so strtod call sites need updating, not just relinking

gotchas: -ffast-math builds break infinity/NaN handling (open issue #397 as of 2026-09-24; no fix merged yet)
Locale-dependent decimal separators (e.g. comma) require the separate from_chars_advanced + parse_options call, not the default from_chars
chars_format::json rejects bare inf/nan by default; use the non-standard json_or_infnan variant to allow them
v8.2.0 had a big-endian regression on s390x (issue #354, closed/fixed) - use a current release rather than pinning that tag if targeting big-endian
pick_this_over_siblings_when: fast_float parses text to binary (beats strtod/std::from_chars); Dragonbox, Ryu, and {fmt} format binary to text (beat sprintf/std::to_chars) - they solve the opposite problem, so pick fast_float for the parsing side of a pipeline and pair it with one of those for the formatting side rather than treating them as substitutes.
verified_claims_summary: Peer-reviewed benchmark (Lemire, Software: Practice and Experience 51(8), 2021) measured fast_float::from_chars against glibc strtod, single-threaded, GCC 10.2 -O3 -DNDEBUG, on an Intel Skylake i7-6700: 45 Mfloat/s vs 9.0 Mfloat/s (5x) on the 111k-line 'canada' JSON coordinate corpus (Table 9); comparable 3-5x wins held on AMD Zen2, ARM Ampere, and IBM POWER9 CPUs, and against MSVC STL's std::from_chars on an Intel i7-7700K (Table 13).
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-23, tagged v8.3.0), triple-licensed Apache-2.0/MIT/BSL-1.0, header-only and small enough to vendor; already embedded in GCC 12's std::from_chars and used by Chromium, WebKit/Safari, MySQL, DuckDB, Boost.JSON, ClickHouse, Blender, and Apache Arrow, which makes it low-risk to adopt.
